column1: # The queue rules, as cases rather than as code.
# docs/PLAN_WEB_LIBRARY.md S1. The rules live twice -- PlayQueue.kt and web/src/rules.js -- because
# a browser cannot run Kotlin, and they will go on living twice. What must not happen twice is
# DECIDING what they are. C23, C30 and C31 were each one screen doing what the other did not, all
# three found by the owner rather than by a test, all three inside a week.
# Neither implementation is the reference. THIS FILE IS. A rule changed on one side and not the
# other fails on the side that did not change, which is the entire mechanism.
# Tab-separated, because that is what everything else in this project reads -- songdb, Modland's
# favourites, the engine's own `describe`. Five lines to parse on each side and no dependency, which
# `org.json` would have been in a unit test that only has a stub of it.
# Shuffle is deliberately absent: the two sides shuffle with different generators, and agreeing on a
# permutation would mean sharing an implementation, which is the thing that cannot be done.
# PlayQueueTest covers it on the Kotlin side.
# A group is [name] followed by a header row and then its cases. `-` means null.

column1: # HVSC's time tokens, which the phone reads in SongLengths.parseTime and the page in
# web/src/songlengths.js. A SID carries no length; the whole feature rests on reading these right,
# and the fraction is the trap -- ".5" is half a second, and the field is described as
# milliseconds in places, so reading it as five milliseconds makes every fractional length wrong by
# up to a second in a way nobody notices from the numbers. `-` means the token is not a time, which
# is the caller's cue to drop the whole line rather than keep a tune with one length missing.
